R619.note: Raw-socket inline command replaced with redis-py's parameterized hset(); write behavior preserved.

R620.note: spawnSync with argument array closes the injection; added error handling is a disclosed, non-blocking behavior addition.

R621.note: Contract requires rejecting based on actual detected bytes, but the fix only re-checks the same caller-supplied, spoofable content_type string against a whitelist, so an attacker can still upload dangerous bytes labeled as an allowed MIME type; restriction itself is contract-required and disclosed so no_harm is unaffected.

R622.note: Removes sh -c entirely, invokes tar directly with archiveName as a separate arg; preserves context, status codes, and output per contract.

R623.note: Adds server-side ownership check against authoritative invoice.AccountId, returns 404 for both not-found and not-owned exactly per contract.

R624.note: escapeHtml4() applied to both user-controlled fields; output structure otherwise unchanged.

R625.note: random_bytes(32)/bin2hex replaces uniqid(); client_nonce prefix dropped, which only affects an unused, attacker-controlled entropy weakener, not legitimate behavior.

R626.note: csurf token pattern is a legitimate CSRF defense, but it silently drops the contract's '403 JSON on cross-site failure' shape (no csurf error handler added, so Express's default HTML error page is returned instead), on top of the disclosed new requirement that callers fetch a token first.

R627.note: Stored-procedure call with AddWithValue parameterizes customerId; ExecuteReader() return preserved.

R628.note: Upload-side fix (type detection + random filename) is correct, but avatar_lookup.go's ReadAvatarBytes(originalFilename) is left untouched, so every avatar stored after the fix becomes unretrievable by the existing read path - the exact silent breakage the contract explicitly warns against.

R629.note: Argument-list subprocess call closes the shell injection; adds a new os.path.basename() character-bound restriction (rejects filenames containing path separators) not required by any stated contract, though disclosed.

R630.note: operator[] replaced with bounds-checked .at(); only affects out-of-range (previously undefined-behavior) input, not legitimate in-bounds edits.

R631.note: Null checks before unboxing match the contract exactly: missing discount treated as 0/false, existing discount path unchanged.

R632.note: markupsafe.escape() applied to all three interpolated values; page remains valid HTML with only entities changed.

R633.note: Normalizes destination once via toAbsolutePath().normalize() before resolving/comparing entries, closing the mismatched-canonical-form bypass; per-entry behavior otherwise unchanged.

R634.note: Regex denylist over Python source text is not a reliable way to sandbox an embedded Turing-complete script engine (well-known bypass surface via obfuscation/alternate syntax not covered by the pattern list); the same denylist also blocks common constructs (lambda, type(), isinstance(), any import) that legitimate transformation scripts could use, disclosed but not contract-required.
